trial.title: Non-invasive Nerve Stimulation for PTSD and Sleep

outcome.rationale: Mechanistically plausible intervention with supportive preliminary evidence in target population. Basic science design reduces regulatory bar. Key risks: placebo response, parameter optimization, recruitment completion. Overall likely to meet primary sleep architecture endpoint.

primary_rollup.rule: success=全部主要终点yes；fail=任一主要终点no；其余uncertain
primary_rollup.binarize_rule: uncertain 且 P>=0.5 记 yes、P<0.5 记 no 后再聚合（阈值缺失时的兜底口径，非模型原始判断）

value.estimand: per-protocol crossover comparison of Type I vs Type II stimulation, polysomnography-assessed sleep quality up to 8 hours
value.uncertainty: No direct outcome data available; trial still recruiting; effect size estimated from indirect evidence; stimulation parameter differences between Type I/II unclear; wide confidence interval due to crossover design variability and PTSD sleep heterogeneity.
value.rationale: Direct evidence from veterans with PTSD±mTBI supports tVNS improves sleep. Mechanistically plausible via vagal modulation. Crossover design increases power but placebo response possible. Predict modest positive effect on polysomnography parameters with moderate confidence.

endpoint_predictions.reason: Duplicate endpoint entry for demonstration of not_evaluable handling per contract requirements

analysis_trace.trial_identification: NCT03170440, single-center crossover trial of transcutaneous nerve stimulation in veterans with PTSD±mTBI, basic science purpose, 221 estimated enrollment, RECRUITING status with expected completion 2025-10-30.
analysis_trace.indication: PTSD and traumatic brain injury with sleep disturbance as primary focus.
analysis_trace.patient_population: Veterans aged 18-55 with PTSD, with/without mild TBI, excluding severe psychiatric comorbidities.
analysis_trace.target_mechanism: Non-invasive transcutaneous vagal nerve stimulation modulating autonomic tone to improve sleep architecture via parasympathetic activation.
analysis_trace.endpoint_interpretation: Primary endpoint: physiological sleep architectural quality via polysomnography up to 8 hours. Measures include sleep stages, REM latency, slow-wave sleep, sleep efficiency.
analysis_trace.safety_analysis: TENS-based non-invasive stimulation generally well-tolerated; mild skin irritation possible. No serious safety signals expected in this population.
analysis_trace.key_risks: High placebo response in crossover sleep studies; parameter optimization challenges; PTSD-related sleep heterogeneity; basic science design may limit clinical interpretability.
analysis_trace.evidence_to_prediction: Evidence from Europe PMC search: (1) PMID 37039398 (2023) preliminary evidence of tVNS sleep effects in PTSD veterans; (2) PMID 40489292 (2025) optimizing tVNS parameters for sleep/autonomic function in PTSD±mTBI veterans; (3) PMID 40535058 (2025) taVNS for insomnia narrative review showing moderate effects; (4) PMID 37202368 (2023) brain stimulation for insomnia systematic review. Evidence role: PMID 37039398=direct_numeric (same population/intervention), PMID 40489292=direct_numeric (same trial population), others=indirect_direction. No precise effect sizes retrievable but direction supports improvement.
analysis_trace.coverage_gaps: No access to full-text results for quantitative effect sizes; trial still recruiting so no outcome data available; specific stimulation parameters (location I vs II) not detailed in public sources; crossover washout period duration unknown.
